item.content:encoded:
Nov 9, 2026, 11:29 AM ET
The Atlanta Braves are "highly unlikely" to trade star outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr. this offseason, per Jon Morosi of MLB Network. Acuna is likely to hit free agency following the 2028 season, as Atlanta holds a club option for 2028 that they will almost certainly pick up. While the Braves may not be interested in paying Acuna what it would require to keep him past 2028, it appears that Atlanta is not entertaining moving him now ahead of 2027. Across 469 plate appearances in 2026, the 28-year-old hit .255/.345/.451 with 20 home runs, 55 RBI, 61 runs scored, and 21 stolen bases. While Acuna remains a productive player, he hasn't quite recaptured the magic of his 2023 season, when he hit 41 home runs and stole 73 bases. Injuries have been a huge part of the story, as Acuna Jr. missed significant time due to hamstring issues in 2026. If he can get back to full health, Acuna has as high a production upside as any player in baseball.--Will Brady
Source: MLB Network - Jon MorosiComments · Join ChatOpen App
More Recent News
Nov 9, 2026, 11:59 AM ET
Across 615 plate appearances in 2026, Atlanta Braves catcher Drake Baldwin hit .284/.358/.459 with 25 home runs, 79 RBI, 85 runs scored, and three stolen bases. The 25-year-old got off to a scorching-hot start to the season before suffering an oblique strain in mid-May that sidelined him for about a month. Baldwin struggled upon his return, hitting just .063 across 50 plate appearances in June after being reinserted into the Braves lineup. However, the young backstop bounced back and closed the season strong, hitting .315 with 10 home runs across 296 plate appearances after the All-Star break. Baldwin's underlying metrics supported his production at the plate, as he posted an excellent 50.9% hard-hit rate and kept his strikeout rate to a manageable 21.5%. Atlanta also frequently used him at designated hitter, both keeping his legs fresh and keeping him in the lineup on an everyday basis. Heading into 2027, Baldwin is in the conversation as the top catcher in fantasy baseball.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Nov 9, 2026, 11:47 AM ET
Since his breakout season in 2024, Kansas City Royals left-hander Cole Ragans (elbow) has basically been a non-factor for fantasy managers. The 28-year-old pitched just 35 1/3 innings (eight starts) in 2026 before hitting the injured list with triceps and elbow soreness. Ragans initially attempted to rehab his arm, but he suffered a setback in June and ultimately underwent an internal brace procedure in July. As a result, Ragans missed the remainder of the 2026 season and will likely miss a significant chunk of 2027 as well. On the bright side, Ragans may finally be able to work his way back to full health and regain his peak form while he rehabs from the surgery. However, the talented southpaw is tough for fantasy managers to trust until he gets back on the mound and proves he can stay healthy for an extended stretch of time.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Nov 9, 2026, 11:39 AM ET
Pittsburgh Pirates shortstop Konnor Griffin had an up-and-down season as a rookie in 2026. The 20-year-old was productive for a very young player when healthy, hitting .272/.324/.404 with six home runs, 33 RBI, 43 runs scored, and 23 stolen bases. However, he spent a significant chunk of the season sidelined by two different injuries, first a flexor strain and then a finger injury. Griffin also struggled to hit for power even when he was on the field, posting just a 6.9% barrel rate and a 37.5% hard-hit rate. Still, Griffin managed to put together a respectable season as a rookie while battling injury issues. If he can get and stay fully healthy in 2027, Griffin could emerge as a true five-category difference-maker for fantasy managers. His profile carries some risk due to the unknown, but Griffin is an ultra-high-upside shortstop bet who could pay off for fantasy managers in a big way in 2027.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Nov 9, 2026, 11:22 AM ET
After initially opening the season in Triple-A, Boston Red Sox left-hander Payton Tolle emerged as arguably his team's best starting pitcher in 2026. Across 148 2/3 innings (26 starts) in the big leagues, Tolle recorded a 9-6 record with a 3.03 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 171 strikeouts. The 24-year-old averaged 96.2 miles per hour on his fastball and struck out 28.4% of the batters he faced while allowing just a 6.6% walk rate. Tolle also only allowed a .624 OPS against right-handed hitters, which will be key for him to continue as he makes his home starts in front of the Green Monster at Fenway Park. Heading into 2027, Tolle has all the makings of a fantasy ace, and he will likely come off the board very early in most drafts.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Bryan Woo a Bounce-Back Candidate in 2027


Will Brady




Nov 9, 2026, 11:14 AM ET
Seattle Mariners starting pitcher Bryan Woo had a disappointing year relative to expectations in 2026, recording a 12-10 record with a 4.01 ERA, 1.10 WHIP, and 175 strikeouts across 173 innings (30 starts). The 26-year-old's production dropped off across the board relative to his 2025 campaign, when he finished fifth in the American League Cy Young Award voting. However, there's plenty of reason for fantasy managers to believe in Woo's ability to bounce back in 2027. Much of Woo's ERA increase can be attributed to his 66.2% strand rate, which was significantly below his 73.4% career mark. Even in a down year, the young right-hander remained an excellent source of WHIP and a solid source of strikeouts, and he's also now logged back-to-back 30-start seasons. Heading into 2027, fantasy managers may want to look to buy low on Woo.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Catcher Testifies in Court Amid MLB Gambling Scandal


Keith Hernandez




Nov 9, 2026, 10:31 AM ET
Catcher Bo Naylor, a former teammate of Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz, testified last Thursday at their sports-betting trial that he did not know gamblers could place bets on individual pitches until the criminal case arose, according to Larry Neumeister of The Associated Press. Clase and Ortiz pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges after they were filed a year ago. Prosecutors said the two pitchers accepted several thousand dollars in payments so sports gamblers could place bets on individual pitches, enabling the gamblers to pocket at least $460,000. Prosecutors say that Clase began giving information about his pitches to bettors in 2023 and recruited Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Clase and Ortiz are both free on bail and are on non-disciplinary leave from the Guardians without pay while facing prosecution. Naylor testified that he was not close friends with either pitcher, and that he would frequently see Clase on his cellular phone in the locker room. Prosecutors have alleged that Clase sometimes broke MLB rules by communicating with gamblers during games.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Associated Press - Larry Neumeister
Cubs Unlikely to Enter Bidding War for Tarik Skubal


Keith Hernandez




Nov 9, 2026, 10:18 AM ET
The Chicago Cubs' priority this offseason is starting pitching, but The Athletic's Sahadev Sharma writes that it is unlikely that the Cubs will enter a bidding war for two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal. The Cubs were aggressive in adding third baseman Alex Bregman to a five-year, $175 million deal last offseason, but they have shied away from the very top of the free-agent market in recent offseasons. Chicago has "shown no interest" in spending like the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets, and it will not be an exception this winter, when labor negotiations will muddy the waters for teams and their finances. The Cubs will, however, check in on other pitches, as they have just one pitcher with legitimate starting experience on their roster who is set to enter 2027 healthy. The goal for the Cubs is likely to bring in three starting pitchers. After their starters allowed the third-most home runs (142) in 2026, the Cubs will target pitchers with high ground-ball rates and/or a high strikeout rate. This means they will most likely attempt to bring back right-hander Clay Holmes, who led baseball with a 60.7% ground-ball rate. Two other potential free-agent fits could be Freddy Peralta and Michael King. For Skubal, it is going to take a large sum of money to secure his services long-term, and the Dodgers and Mets will be the front-runners.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Sahadev Sharma
Corbin Carroll has Offseason Elbow Surgery


Keith Hernandez




Nov 9, 2026, 10:09 AM ET
Arizona Diamondbacks outfielder Corbin Carroll (elbow) had offseason elbow surgery last Thursday to remove loose bodies, according to Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic. Carroll is expected to maintain a normal offseason program and should be a full-go for spring training next year. The All-Star outfielder and former National League Rookie of the Year said he felt "a little bit" of discomfort in his elbow during the season, but it worsened last week. He said he has a minimally invasive NanoScope procedure, which is the same one that left-hander Tarik Skubal had when he was still with the Detroit Tigers last season that allowed him to return from the injured list in only six weeks. Carroll said he is hoping to start swinging a bat again at the start of December. Piecoro notes that the bigger issue for Carroll in 2026 was his back. He is trying to put himself in better positions in the weight room to avoid similar problems in the future. The 26-year-old also had a hamate procedure on his hand at the start of spring training, and he hit .239/.328/.467 with 22 homers, 33 doubles, and 17 triples while stealing 21 bases in 582 at-bats. It was definitely a drop after Carroll had 31 homers, 84 RBI, and 32 steals in 2025, but he has at least 22 homers and 21 stolen bases in each of the last four years.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Arizona Republic - Nick Piecoro
Seiya Suzuki Receives Qualifying Offer From Cubs


Keith Hernandez




Nov 6, 2026, 11:14 AM ET
As expected, outfielder Seiya Suzuki received a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer from the Chicago Cubs, according to Joel Sherman of the New York Post. Suzuki will almost certainly decline the offer and enter the free-agent market this winter as one of the top free-agent outfield bats available. It remains to be seen if Chicago is serious about re-signing the 32-year-old, who had another strong season in 2026 in his fifth year in the majors, slashing .270/.368/.473 with an .841 OPS, 26 home runs, 86 RBI, 96 runs scored, and three stolen bases in 143 games across 634 plate appearances. Suzuki sold out for power in 2025 with a career-low .245 batting average (140-for-571), but he did produce career highs in home runs (32) and RBI (103) in 151 regular-season games played. In addition to being a consistent power bat in the outfield, Suzuki has graded out well defensively in right field, which will make him even more attractive on the open market this offseason. If he declines the Cubs' qualifying offer (he should), the Cubs will receive draft-pick compensation if he signs elsewhere.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Post - Joel Sherman
Jacob Young, Nationals Agree to Four-Year Extension


Keith Hernandez




Nov 6, 2026, 11:06 AM ET
Outfielder Jacob Young and the Washington Nationals agreed to a four-year, $23 million contract extension on Friday that includes an $8 million option for a fifth season, a source familiar with the deal told Robert Murray of FanSided. The deal helps the Nats avoid salary arbitration for the first time with Young. The 27-year-old is more glove and speed than bat, as he is considered one of the better defensive center fielders in the game. Although the former seventh-rounder in 2021 from the University of Florida does not have much power at the plate, he does have enough speed to make him fantasy-relevant in deeper leagues. Young stole a career-high 33 bases for the Nats in his first full season in 2024 and has at least 15 steals in the last two seasons. The 2026 campaign was one of his better showings at the plate, hitting .252/.318/.390 with a career-high .707 OPS, a career-high 10 home runs, 50 RBI, 57 runs scored, and 18 stolen bases in 140 games across 471 plate appearances. Fantasy managers seeking power from an outfielder will want to avoid Young, as he has hit just 15 home runs in his four big-league seasons since debuting with Washington in 2023.--Keith Hernandez
Source: FanSided - Robert Murray
Albert Pujols to Interview for Astros' Managerial Job


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 10:30 PM ET
Future Hall of Fame first baseman Albert Pujols will interview for the Houston Astros' managerial vacancy on Thursday, sources told Alden Gonzalez of ESPN. The Astros named former St. Louis Cardinals executive Randy Flores as their new general manager five days ago. Flores spent eight years in the big leagues before joining St. Louis' front office, with five of those years spent as Pujols' teammate in St. Louis, including a World Series championship in 2006. Pujols has made it clear that he has a desire to manage in the big leagues, and he won a championship in the Dominican winter league in his first season leading the Leones del Escogido in January of 2025 while also serving as the skipper for the Dominican Republic in this year's World Baseball Classic, where his squad lost to the United States in the semifinals. Pujols was a finalist for the managerial openings in the last hiring cycle with the Los Angeles Angels and San Diego Padres. New York Yankees bench coach Brad Ausmus is also among those being considered by the Astros for their managerial position.--Keith Hernandez
Source: ESPN.com - Alden Gonzalez
Padres Extend Qualifying Offer to Adrian Morejon


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 10:10 PM ET
The San Diego Padres extended a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer to left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon, according to the New York Post's Joel Sherman. The 27-year-old hard-throwing southpaw is expected to decline the offer and become one of the top relievers available in his prime. Morejon has until Nov. 17 to accept or decline the offer. The Padres chose not to extend a qualifying offer to first baseman Ty France. Morejon, who hits triple digits on the radar gun regularly with his fastball and has pinpoint control, had a strong 2.83 ERA over 76 relief outings this year after posting a 2.08 ERA in 2025. If Morejon declines the offer, as expected, and signs elsewhere, the Padres would receive a compensatory draft pick. The Padres will have one of the better bullpens in baseball again in 2027, even if Morejon does not return, but they are definitely interested in a reunion. Morejon also expressed a desire to return at the end of the season. "Everybody knows that," Morejon said of his desire to return. "My agent knows that. It's not really in my hands right now." Morejon could have a chance to be a full-time closer if he tests the market, though, but in San Diego, he would remain a late-inning setup man in front of Mason Miller.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Post - Joel Sherman
Jake Bauers Receives Qualifying Offer From Brewers


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 10:02 PM ET
First baseman/outfielder Jake Bauers received a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer from the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, according to Joel Sherman of the New York Post. Of the eight players who were extended qualifying offers by their respective teams, Bauers is the most surprising. The 31-year-old left-handed slugger had a strong year in 2026 and definitely played a key role in helping the Brewers capture their first-ever World Series title, but coming into this season, he had never produced more than 12 home runs in a single season in six years in the big leagues. In 144 games and 578 plate appearances with the Brew Crew during the regular season, Bauers hit .266/.389/.484 with a career-best .874 OPS, 26 home runs, 86 RBI, 93 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases. He had a career slash line of .208/.302/.361 at the end of the 2024 season and came close to hanging up his cleats. Bauers tapped into a side we had never seen before this year, walking at a 16.3% clip, with only six qualified hitters having a higher wRC+ than Bauers. He was named the National League Championship Series MVP and could serve as the Brewers' primary first baseman in 2027 if he accepts the qualifying offer, which he is expected to do.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Post - Joel Sherman
Ryan Jeffers Receives Qualifying Offer From Twins


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 9:47 PM ET
Catcher Ryan Jeffers received a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer from the Minnesota Twins, according to Dan Hayes of The Athletic. Jeffers has until Nov. 17 to accept it or decline it. Jeffers, who is about to enter his age-30 campaign, has been one of the more productive catchers in baseball in the last few seasons. The former second-rounder in 2018 from the University of North Carolina at Wilmington played in only 92 games due to injuries in the first half of the year in his seventh season with the Twins in 2026, but he was still very productive, slashing .256/.353/.461 with an .814 OPS, 14 home runs, 56 RBI, 49 runs scored, and a stolen base in 369 plate appearances. Most players who are extended a qualifying offer end up rejecting it to seek more riches on the open market, but it could be hard for Jeffers to turn this one-year deal down. If Jeffers turns the offer down and goes to the open market, he will be one of the most sought-after offensive-minded catchers of the offseason. Jeffers had a career-high 21 home runs and 64 RBI a couple of seasons ago in 2024, but he also hit just .226 that year with a .300 on-base percentage.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Dan Hayes
Pirates Extend Qualifying Offer to Brandon Lowe


Keith Hernandez




Nov 4, 2026, 9:28 PM ET
The Pittsburgh Pirates extended a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer to second baseman Brandon Lowe, according to Alex Stumpf. Lowe has until Nov. 17 to accept or deny it. If he denies and signs elsewhere, the Pirates will get a draft pick. The Pirates and Lowe can still negotiate other contracts. It is only the third time since the inception of the qualifying offer in 2012 that the Pirates have chosen to offer it to a player. Pittsburgh acquired the power-hitting second baseman last offseason in a three-team deal that involved the Tampa Bay Rays and Houston Astros. Not only did Lowe fortify his defense at second base in 2026 to become a Gold Glove finalist for the first time in his career, but he also played in a career-high 150 games while recording a career-best 5.4 wins above replacement. Offensively, he flourished in the Steel City, picking up 96 RBI and an .824 OPS while leading all second basemen with 35 home runs. Lowe is expected to decline the one-year qualifying offer for a more lucrative multi-year deal on the open market. The two-time All-Star now has two straight 30-homer seasons (three in his career) and has some of the best pop among second basemen, but it remains to be seen if he will be able to stay healthy in his 10th year in the big leagues in 2027.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Alex Stumpf
Nov 3, 2026, 9:14 PM ET
Tampa Bay Rays right-handed reliever Edwin Uceta (shoulder) underwent an arthroscopic procedure on his right shoulder in October and will miss at least the first couple of months of the 2027 season, president of baseball operations Erik Neander told Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times. Uceta was set to enter the 2026 campaign as Tampa's primary ninth-inning option, but that all changed when he dealt with a right-shoulder impingement and never pitched for the Rays at all last season. Bryan Baker ended up taking over closing duties for Tampa and led all of baseball with 41 saves and a 1.44 ERA to help the team get back to the World Series, where they lost in five games to the Milwaukee Brewers. Uceta will now miss the start of next season as well, and when he returns, he will most likely be relegated to a high-leverage setup role in front of Baker. The 28-year-old Dominican hurler combined to go 12-3 with a 2.98 ERA (2.98 FIP), 1.04 WHIP, six saves, 160 strikeouts, and 35 walks in 117 2/3 relief innings over 100 appearances out of the bullpen in his first two seasons for the Rays in 2024 and 2025. There is no guarantee that Uceta will be as dominant a high-leverage bullpen arm when he returns from his shoulder issues.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Tampa Bay Times - Marc Topkin
Jazz Chisholm Jr. Not Expected Back in the Bronx


Keith Hernandez




Nov 3, 2026, 8:58 PM ET
ESPN's Jorge Castillo writes that both New York Yankees infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. and outfielder Trent Grisham "are as good as gone" for next season, so the Yankees will need to figure out second base and center field. Chisholm was one of the notable names this year not to be given a $23.15 million qualifying offer, so the Yankees will not receive draft-pick compensation when he leaves in free agency. Chisholm was an All-Star for the second time in his career in 2025 in his first full season with the Bombers, clubbing 31 home runs, driving in 80 runs, and stealing 31 bases in only 130 regular-season games, but he could not match that production in his seventh year in the big leagues. The 28-year-old left-handed slugger struggled to a .231 batting average (109-for-471) with 19 home runs, 55 RBI, and a 29.5% strikeout rate in 532 regular-season plate appearances, but he did manage to steal a career-high 41 bases. On the open market this offseason, Chisholm will be one of the most coveted power/speed threats among position players, but a move away from New York's short porch in right field could hurt his overall power ceiling in fantasy baseball.--Keith Hernandez
Source: ESPN.com - Jorge Castillo
Teoscar Hernandez an Obvious Trade Candidate for Dodgers


Keith Hernandez




Nov 3, 2026, 8:45 PM ET
ESPN's Buster Olney writes that veteran outfielder Teoscar Hernandez is the Los Angeles Dodgers' most obvious trade candidate this offseason as they look to reshape their position-player group to get younger and more athletic. As Hernandez gets older and his defensive skills decline, there is no place for him at designated hitter in L.A., with the presence of Shohei Ohtani. Not only does Hernandez's defense in left field continue to decline, but he was also a disappointment at the plate in 2026 after signing a three-year, $66 million contract with the Blue last offseason. The 34-year-old Dominican native saw a sharp drop in power and hit .267/.334/.425 with a .759 OPS, 16 home runs, 64 RBI, 66 runs scored, five stolen bases, 135 strikeouts, and 42 walks in 125 games played and 491 plate appearances during the regular season. The two-time All-Star hit a combined 58 home runs and drove in 188 runs during the regular season in his first two years with the Dodgers while helping them win back-to-back championships. The writing is on the wall for Hernandez to be traded away, which would be a big hit to his fantasy value.--Keith Hernandez
Source: ESPN - Buster Olney
Yankees Plan to Bring Giancarlo Stanton to Spring Training


Keith Hernandez




Nov 3, 2026, 8:36 PM ET
There has been speculation as to whether the New York Yankees would cut oft-injured outfielder/designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton this offseason, but YES Network's Jack Curry said that the Yankees will bring Stanton to spring training next year to see what he has left in the tank. If the 36-year-old five-time All-Star and former MVP struggles in spring training or is still injured, the Yankees could move on then. He is entering the final year of his 13-year, $325 million deal with the Yankees and is owed $15 million in 2027 ($10 million buyout), with a $15 million club option for the 2028 season, which is expected to be declined. General manager Brian Cashman said that Stanton finished the 2026 season healthy, but he managed to play in only 24 games in his 17th year in the league while slashing .256/.302/.422 with a .724 OPS, three home runs, 14 RBI, eight runs scored, and a 29:6 K:BB in 96 plate appearances. In 2025, Stanton played in only 77 games. Stanton has become a major injury liability and could find himself on the free-agent market early next year if he cannot get back on the field and stay there.--Keith Hernandez
Source: YES Network - Jack Curry
MLB Proposes Delaying Salary Cap Until 2028


Keith Hernandez




Nov 3, 2026, 8:26 PM ET
Major League Baseball proposed postponing the implementation of a salary cap until the 2028 season on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Jeff Passan, as the current collective bargaining agreement approaches its Dec. 1 expiration. The league has pressed forward with its pursuit of a cap and floor despite the Players Association voicing its objection to any cap. The $258.2 million cap and $180.2 million floor that MLB projected for 2028 were higher than the $245.3 million and $171.2 million numbers that the league proposed as its original cap-and-floor offer for 2027. MLB also proposed giving $282 million in competitive balance tax proceeds to players in cash payments, according to sources. Union officials have said that players would lose more than $1 billion over the life of the league's proposal if they agreed to a cap. The last time MLB formally proposed a cap-and-floor system in 1994, players went on strike for 232 days, and the World Series was canceled. Under the 2028 cap-and-floor projections, 12 teams, including the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, would need to increase their payrolls to reach the floor. Eight teams carried payrolls that would have been in excess of the ceiling. The MLBPA has proposed maintaining the current framework of the league's financial system while increasing spending, and the union has also asked for a surge in the minimum salary from $780,000 to $1.5 million and free agency for players 30 and older after five years of major-league service, not six.--Keith Hernandez
Source: ESPN.com - Jeff Passan

item.content:encoded:
Bobby Witt Jr. becomes the first three-time winner of the Heart and Hustle Award.
Created by the MLBPAA in 2005, the Heart & Hustle Award recognizes an active player who demonstrates a passion for baseball and best embodies the values, spirit and traditions of the game. Each of the 30 teams has one nominee selected by a committee of former players, with fans, alumni and active Major League players voting to determine the overall winner.
Witt has been Kansas City's nominee in each of his first five Major League seasons, establishing himself as one of the game's top all-around players while also making an impact in the clubhouse and community.
David Lesky has more on new Royals assistant hitting coach Hunter Mense.
He's very big on pre-pitch planning. Go to the plate with a plan, and it's much easier to execute than without one. That lets a hitter jump into good counts or lay off the pitch they should lay off. With that, he's done an excellent job throughout his career of helping hitters with a variety of swings because the 3-0 swing shouldn't be the same as the 0-2 swing, which shouldn't be the same as the 1-1 swing. Situational awareness is the biggest thing.
I didn't have much conversation about Mense after the hire was announced, but I did talk to a couple of people who noted how great he is on the mental side of the game. That probably shouldn't be a surprise given that he has a Master's degree in Counseling Psychology with an emphasis in sport psychology. It's an interesting profile given that the Royals chose to reassign Melissa Lambert, the previous director of behavioral science/Major League mental performance. I'm still under the impression they plan to hire someone else for the dugout for that role, but the fact that Mense has that educational background is interesting to me.
Philip Ruo at Royals Keep writes about eight free agents the Royals should target, such as Taylor Ward.
Ward is another player who took a major step back in production after being traded and is the 67th-ranked free agent. Ward posted an 117 wRC+ in Baltimore, which fell to 23 with the Mariners after the trade. Even before his disastrous trade, Ward's power had evaporated. After hitting 36 home runs in 663 plate appearances in 2025 with the Angels, Ward hit only seven homers in 506 PAs with Baltimore (and at a more homer-friendly ballpark) and zero homers in Seattle.
Interestingly, despite his dip in home runs, his .336 wOBA in Baltimore was roughly the same as his .339 wOBA in 2025. This was largely due to his increase in walk rate from 11.3% to 16.3% and a decrease in strikeout rate from 26.4% to 20.4%. If Ward can combine his increased plate discipline with a revival of his power, he could be a valuable addition to the Royals, especially as a right-handed batter. He would likely also be willing to sign a one-year prove-it deal to increase his value, and the Royals could be beneficiaries of this opportunity.
The White Sox signed former Royals pitcher Alec Marsh to a minor league deal.
The Royals acquired a 28-story office building near Crown Center to lease out as office space.

Trade season is upon us. Here are potential targets for the Phillies to address their big needs.
As baseball descends on Las Vegas for the GM meetings Monday, the trade market might be stimulated by the compressed offseason. Let's look at four players who could be fits with the Phillies.
Executives from 30 major league front offices will walk into a Las Vegas resort and casino Monday evening for the annual general managers’ meetings.
That’s a lot of poker faces.
But with the owners poised to lock out the players upon the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, the meetings could serve as the launching pad for a three-week free-agent frenzy.
That’s how it happened five years ago. With baseball barreling toward a labor fight, teams spent a total of nearly $2 billion on free agents in the weeks before the owners locked out the players.
» READ MORE: A (likely long) lockout looms again for MLB. Why a salary cap is at the center of it all. Again.
Tarik Skubal is easily the headliner of this free-agent class, but if the two-time Cy Young Award winner signs before the lockout, he won’t be alone. Fellow starting pitchers Michael King, Freddy Peralta, and Clay Holmes, and relievers Adrian Morejon and David Bednar could come off the board, too.
The Phillies are interested in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, multiple sources confirmed, likely as a left fielder even though he played mostly third base in Japan. But two non-Phillies talent evaluators said they graded him as a below-average defender at every position.
Sato, who turns 28 in March, also bats left-handed. Coupled with the defensive questions, that could leave the Phillies to favor a pair of righty-hitting outfielders entering their age-32 seasons with nearly identical five-year numbers, including batting average/on-base/slugging slash lines and Fangraphs’ WAR:
- Seiya Suzuki: .269/.351/.472, 113 homers, 24.8% strikeout rate, 128 OPS+, 15.6 WAR in 675 games
- Randy Arozarena: .251/.348/.434, 116 homers, 24.6% strikeout rate, 124 OPS+, 16.2 WAR in 772 games
Suzuki and Arozarena are likely in line for similar four- or five-year contracts. And because both received the free-agent qualifying offer, signing them would involve draft-pick compensation. But either player would boost a Phillies lineup that this season was 26th in OPS from outfielders (.686), 29th from the cleanup spot (.645), and 30th from the right side of the plate (.658).
The Phillies have other needs, too, and with roughly $280 million in luxury-tax commitments for 2027, president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski won’t be able to throw money at all of them.
It’s possible the trade market will also be stimulated by the compressed offseason calendar, officials from multiple clubs suggested this week.
The GM meetings are usually a time when teams lay the groundwork for activity later in the offseason. But with limited time to make deals, and every front office under one roof for two days this week, it could be fertile ground for accelerated trade talks.
(History lesson: The Phillies famously traded for closer Brad Lidge at the GM meetings in 2007.)
Let’s focus on four players who may be available for various reasons and would potentially fit the Phillies’ roster:
Steven Kwan
A few days before the trade deadline in 2025, the Guardians were under .500 and reeling from the news that star closer Emmanuel Clase would be out indefinitely as the subject of an investigation into his involvement in a sports-betting scheme.
So, they began listening to offers for Kwan.
The Phillies tried to trade for the All-Star left fielder, major league sources said at the time. But with Kwan under club control through 2027, Cleveland kept him and was rewarded with a late surge to the AL Central title — and another division crown this year. (The Phillies instead acquired center fielder Harrison Bader from the Twins.)
» READ MORE: Will the Phillies spend to beef up the middle of the order? Here are some free-agent options.
Rival team officials believe Kwan may be available again given the low-payroll Guardians’ history of trading stars as they enter their last year before free agency. They dealt Corey Kluber after the 2019 season, Francisco Lindor in January 2021, and Josh Naylor three years later. It’s how the Guardians remain competitive — and they’ve made the playoffs in eight of 11 seasons.
If Kwan, projected to make $11.3 million next year, is next to go, the Phillies should remain interested.
The 29-year-old is a contact-hitting, on-base machine who has reached base at a .357 clip, including a career-best .382 mark this season, with a 9.5% strikeout rate. He’s cut from a similar mold as Luis Arraez with two notable differences: He swings less than Arraez and walks almost twice as often. Like Arraez, Kwan would be a counterweight to the Phillies’ swing-and-miss tendencies.
Kwan is also a four-time Gold Glove-winning left fielder and above average in center. The Phillies could reimagine the outfield by signing Suzuki or Arozarena, trading for Kwan, giving Justin Crawford the majority of the at-bats in center field, and trading Brandon Marsh for a reliever or backup catcher.
The Guardians were reportedly believed to be seeking top-100 prospects for Kwan in 2025. With only one year of control, the return figures to be lower now. Start here: Change-of-scenery-candidate reliever Orion Kerkering and a couple of positional prospects from among Aroon Escobar, Bryan Rincon, Dante Nori, and Gabriel Rincones Jr.
Isaac Paredes
A year ago, the Astros reportedly discussed swapping Paredes for Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran. It didn’t materialize, and they went into the season with an infield surplus that came in handy when third baseman Carlos Correa tore an ankle tendon in May.
But Correa is expected to be healthy to begin next season, leaving new general manager Randy Flores with a familiar problem: Too many infielders.
The Astros exercised Paredes’ $13.35 million option but could still choose to unload him (or shortstop Jeremy Peña, also entering his walk year) and add to another area of the roster.
» READ MORE: With help from TB12, Aidan Miller is healthy, grateful for adversity, and primed to impact the Phillies in 2027
Paredes, 27, has right-handed power with 115 homers over the last five seasons, including 25 this year. He’s also patient at the plate (11% career walk rate) and tends to put the ball in play, making him a fit to bat behind Bryce Harper. He would slot in at third base, replacing free agent Alec Bohm and facilitating Bryson Stott’s return to second.
One potential complication: Trading for Paredes could block top prospect Aidan Miller — unless Trea Turner moves to the outfield.
(Worth noting: In discussing a position change for Turner, Dombrowski said last month that the $300 million shortstop “prefers the infield.”)
In any case, it’s not clear that the Phillies and Astros would match up in a trade. Houston owner Jim Crane has little tolerance for rebuilding, and the Astros are reportedly seeking starting pitching and outfielders.
Jordan Hicks
For a bullpen that ranked 21st in the majors in ERA, the seats are filling up quickly alongside Phillies star closer Jhoan Duran.
Right-handers Alex McFarlane, Jonathan Bowlan, and Caleb Kilian are ticketed for spots. The Phillies re-signed lefty Tim Mayza after the season and will add a high-leverage lefty to replace José Alvarado. (Free-agent options include Morejon and Alex Vesia.) And they could collect a handful of optionable relievers to fill the final two spots.
But setup man Brad Keller, last offseason’s big bullpen addition, is expected to miss all or most of 2027 after Tommy John elbow surgery. It’s fair to wonder if McFarlane (19 major league appearances) and Kilian (57) are sufficient replacements for Keller and likely Kerkering, whose second-half struggles landed him back in triple A and firmly on the trade market.
The Phillies went after Hicks in free agency three years ago but were rebuffed when he accepted the Giants’ offers of four years, $44 million, and a chance to start. He bounced from starting back to relieving — and from San Francisco to Boston to Chicago — before winding up as a veteran in the upstart White Sox’s young bullpen. He will make $12 million in the last year of his contract.
At age 30, Hicks still throws as hard as ever (average fastball velocity: 99.2 mph). Phillies pitching coach Caleb Cotham loves a good sweeper, and Hicks’ is a weapon against right-handed hitters (.161 opposing batting average). Cotham’s challenge would be to rein in a walk rate that ballooned to 15.3%.
But the electric stuff might be worth the dice roll.
Freddy Fermin
Ethan Salas, who made his major league debut Sept. 2 and won’t turn 21 until next June, was behind the plate for three of the Padres’ postseason games. The other three were started by Luis Campusano.
Where does that leave Freddy Fermin?
The Phillies are looking for a more capable backup to help lighten J.T. Realmuto’s league-leading workload. Defense is a high priority, according to Dombrowski, especially because the bar is low to match the combined .316 OPS from Rafael Marchán and Garrett Stubbs. The Phillies outrighted Stubbs last week.
» READ MORE: What the World Series teams and one stellar August can show the Phillies about improving in 2027
Fermin, 31, led Padres catchers with 74 starts in the regular season but slipped to third-string on the depth chart after batting .203 with a .589 OPS. He’s a better hitter (.251 career average, .665 OPS), though his strength is his defense.
Since 2023, Fermin is tied for second among all catchers in defensive runs saved (45) and eighth in fielding run value. He gets high marks for blocking and pop time on throws to second base.
“We do emphasize defense more in our catching position than we do offense,” Dombrowski said. “And a lot of times, if you’re talking about having somebody who can hit and be a good defensive person, it’d be probably an everyday catcher somewhere because they’re not that easy to find.”
Fermin might fit the description.

item.content:encoded:
Federal prosecutors made several aggressive opening remarks during Wednesday’s start of the gambling fraud trial of Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz.
“The defendants, Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz, are cheaters,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Rebecca Urquiola told jurors.
Prosecutors allege the pitchers threw intentional pitches to help gamblers win Major League Baseball prop bets. The gamblers allegedly bet on individual pitches, including whether they would be balls or strikes and how fast the pitches would travel, according to the New York Daily News.
Prosecutors say the alleged scheme led to at least $460,000 in winnings and that they have text messages as evidence. Both pitchers have pleaded not guilty and are currently on unpaid leave from MLB.
Prosecutors Claim Guardians Pitchers Used Secret Codes To Rig Bets
The alleged scheme began in 2023, after Emmanuel Clase, 28, became involved with a Dominican gambler, Enoc Pena.
Prosecutors allege that Clase told Pena what pitches he would throw, allowing gamblers to bet on whether pitches would be balls or strikes and how fast he would throw them. Luis Ortiz, 27, allegedly became involved with the scheme in 2025.
In October 2025, one MLB insider claimed, “Clase will never pitch in MLB again. The gambling evidence found against him is irrefutable.” Federal prosecutors also previously identified 18 pitches they believe Emmanuel Clase deliberately manipulated.
Defense Lawyers Say The Gambling Allegations Are Based On Lies
The Athletic reports that prosecutors say text messages containing words like “chicken” and “rooster” were actually coded communications about rigged pitches and bets.
“He wanted a cut, too. Clase agreed to throw rigged pitches for kickbacks, and that’s exactly what happened,” Urquiola said. “Then Clase brought in a partner, his fellow teammate and pitcher, Luis Ortiz.”
Emmanuel Clase’s lawyer, Michael Bronson, claims Enoc Pena was just a shady gambler who exploited their friendship. He said Pena guessed what pitches Clase would throw and told other gamblers he had insider knowledge.
Regarding the chicken and rooster texts, Bronson said they were about cockfighting in the Dominican Republic, where it’s legal.
Luis Ortiz’s lawyer, Samuel Landes, pointed out that prosecutors have found only two suspected pitches relating to his client.
“That’s not a conspiracy. That’s just baseball,” Landes told the jury, according to FOX 8.
Strangely, prosecutors also do not plan to call Enoc Pena to testify at the trial, despite his alleged role in the scheme.
“Whether he testifies or not, the government’s case is going to depend on Mr. Pena,” Bronson told jurors. “Mr. Pena is an admitted gambling addict. He is a proven, serial liar.”

item.content:encoded:
Avanza caso Guardians: Señalan a Emmanuel Clase y Luis Ortiz por vender información de sus lanzamientos
Los abogados defensores argumentan que los peloteros dominicanos fueron víctimas de engaños por parte de un apostador profesional.
Los lanzadores de los Cleveland Guardians, Emmanuel Clase y Luis Ortiz, fueron señalados como “tramposos” por la fiscalía este miércoles durante los alegatos de apertura en un juicio penal por fraude en Nueva York, caso que ha puesto bajo la lupa la amenaza que representan los apostadores en el béisbol de las Grandes Ligas.
La fiscal federal adjunta, Rebecca Urquiola, dijo a un jurado en Brooklyn que Clase entabló amistad con un apostador deportivo en la República Dominicana a principios de 2023, compartiendo afición por los dominós y las peleas de gallos.
Según la parte acusadora, Clase aceptó informarle sobre el tipo de lanzamientos que realizaría en determinados encuentros, lo que permitió a los apostadores obtener ganancias de al menos 460,000 dólares en plataformas de apuestas en vivo.
“Los acusados, Emmanuel Clase y Luis Ortiz, son unos tramposos. Vendieron sus lanzamientos”, declaró Urquiola ante los jurados.
Las acusaciones de la fiscalía y los detalles de la red
El excerrador estrella de los Guardians y el abridor Ortiz se han declarado no culpables de los cargos de conspiración y se encuentran con licencia sin goce de sueldo desde que fueron arrestados en noviembre de 2025.
La fiscalía sostiene que Clase comenzó a proveer información sobre sus lanzamientos a los apostadores en 2023 y posteriormente reclutó a Ortiz dentro del esquema durante la temporada 2025.
Urquiola detalló que existen mensajes de texto donde los serpentineros describían los pitcheos arreglados utilizando palabras clave como "pollo" o "gallo", evidencia que sumada a los testimonios comprobará la responsabilidad de los peloteros.
Afirman que fueron víctimas de engaño
Por su parte, los abogados defensores argumentaron que sus clientes son inocentes y que el apostador involucrado, identificado como Enoc Peña, se aprovechó de la cercanía con Clase para inventar información y vendérsela a otros apostadores.
Michael Bronson, abogado de Clase, señaló que el relevista era una superestrella de 25 años en 2023 cuando conoció a Peña, un apostador de 41 años con un historial de engaños que vio en el jugador una oportunidad de negocio.
Afirmó además que el apostador perdió más de 200 apuestas intentando adivinar los lanzamientos.
En tanto, Samuel Landes, representante legal de Luis Ortiz, indicó al jurado que el lanzador no tuvo contacto con los apostadores y que el caso en su contra se reduce únicamente a dos lanzamientos marcados como bolas.
“Eso no es una conspiración. Eso es simplemente béisbol”, expresó Landes tras cuestionar por qué Ortiz arriesgaría una carrera millonaria por un pago de 5,000 dólares.
El proceso judicial continuará en los próximos días en la corte de Brooklyn, donde se determinará la situación legal de ambos peloteros caribeños.

item.content:encoded:
Ex-Guardians Pitchers Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz Begin Federal Fraud Trial
Former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz go to trial Monday on charges that they accepted bribes as they colluded with gamblers who made hundreds of thousands of dollars betting correctly on individual pitches.
Their careers and possibly their freedom are at stake in the jury trial expected to unfold over the next month in Brooklyn federal court. Several professional baseball players, including catchers and baseball executives, are among witnesses expected to testify.
Clase, the Guardians’ former closer, and Ortiz, a starter, have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges and are on nondisciplinary leave from the club without pay while their fate is determined.
According to an indictment, the pitchers accepted several thousand dollars in payoffs to help two gamblers from their native Dominican Republic win at least $460,000 on in-game prop bets on the speed and outcome of certain pitches.
Before his trial, Emmanuel Clase spent years in the majors as one of baseball’s most dominant closers, earning three All-Star selections and two AL Reliever of the Year awards in Cleveland. (Photo by Tanner Gatlin/MLB Photos via Getty Images)
Prosecutors allege that Clase began providing the bettors with information about his pitches in 2023 and recruited Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Lawyers for Ortiz unsuccessfully sought to have Ortiz tried separately from Clase.
Judge Kiyo A. Matsumoto said at a conference Friday that she hopes to complete jury selection quickly enough that lawyers can deliver relatively short opening statements in the afternoon.
Clase, 28, is a three-time All-Star and two-time American League Reliever of the Year who had completed his fourth season of a $20 million, five-year contract when charges against the pitchers were revealed in November 2025.
Ortiz, 27, had earned $782,600 as a starting pitcher for the Guardians during the 2025 season.
The pitchers have been charged with wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, money laundering conspiracy and conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery.
Defense lawyers are expected to argue that the pitchers did not collude with gamblers and instead were varying the placement of pitches strategically to fool batters.
On Friday, the judge ruled that prosecutors cannot show the jury proof that Clase owed $500,000 in U.S. taxes because they had only provided the evidence to defense lawyers several days earlier and long after a deadline had passed to turn over evidence to their adversaries.
A prosecutor had argued that the government wanted to put the evidence in the trial to offset any claim by Clase's lawyers that he had no incentive to collude with gamblers because he had several million dollars in financial accounts in the Dominican Republic.
Major League Baseball and the Guardians have both said they've fully cooperated with authorities. MLB has said it contacted federal law enforcement when it began investigating unusual betting activity.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.content:encoded:
Which current players may be potential witnesses during Guardians' Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz trial? appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The federal trial involving Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz is expected to feature testimony from several prominent MLB figures, including current players, team executives and league officials. Among the potential witnesses identified in court-related documents are Guardians general manager Mike Chernoff, assistant general manager Matt Forman, pitching coach Carl Willis and coach/interpreter Agustin Rivero, per The Athletic.
Current and former Cleveland catchers Austin Hedges, Mike Zunino and Bo Naylor have also been identified as potential witnesses. All three catchers were involved in receiving pitches that prosecutors allege were manipulated as part of the betting scheme. However, the actual witness lists remain under seal, and it is not yet established which individuals will ultimately testify.
Regardless, an MLB monitor had initially notified Matt Forman that Clase was using his cellphone in the clubhouse during a game, violating league policy. Forman subsequently reported the incident to MLB.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Quest Meeks, who leads MLB's policy, integrity and compliance division, is also among the identified potential witnesses. Meeks previously testified as a prosecution witness in the federal case involving former Los Angeles Dodgers player Yasiel Puig in January.
Paul Mifsud, MLB's head baseball operations counsel, is also listed. The government identified a total of 42 potential witnesses in proposed jury-selection questions, with the final list expected to be announced later.
The financial allegations are substantial. According to the prosecution, bettors involved in the arrangement generated more than $450,000 in profits through wagers connected to Clase's pitches.
The trial will determine whether Clase and Ortiz deliberately manipulated pitches to help bettors profit, or whether the alleged suspicious pitches were legitimate baseball strategy. With both pitchers pleading not guilty and MLB awaiting the outcome of its investigation, the case could have significant consequences for their careers.
